segments.id: he:The Cycle of Life/Birkat HaMazon in a House of Mourning:1
segments.html: רַבּוֹתַי, נְבָרֵךְ.

segments.id: he:The Cycle of Life/Birkat HaMazon in a House of Mourning:2
segments.html: יְהִי שֵׁם יהוה מְבֹרָךְ מֵעַתָּה וְעַד־עוֹלָם׃

segments.id: he:The Cycle of Life/Birkat HaMazon in a House of Mourning:3
segments.html:
יְהִי שֵׁם יהוה מְבֹרָךְ מֵעַתָּה וְעַד־עוֹלָם׃
בִּרְשׁוּת רַבּוֹתַי, נְבָרֵךְ מְנַחֵם אֲבֵלִים שֶׁאָכַֽלְנוּ מִשֶּׁלּוֹ.

segments.id: he:The Cycle of Life/Birkat HaMazon in a House of Mourning:4
segments.html: בָּרוּךְ מְנַחֵם אֲבֵלִים, שֶׁאָכַֽלְנוּ מִשֶּׁלּוֹ וּבְטוּבוֹ חָיִֽינוּ.

segments.id: he:The Cycle of Life/Birkat HaMazon in a House of Mourning:6
segments.html: בָּרוּךְ מְנַחֵם אֲבֵלִים, וּמְבֹרָךְ שְׁמוֹ תָּמִיד לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד.

segments.id: he:The Cycle of Life/Birkat HaMazon in a House of Mourning:7
segments.html: בָּרוּךְ מְנַחֵם אֲבֵלִים, שֶׁאָכַֽלְנוּ מִשֶּׁלּוֹ וּבְטוּבוֹ חָיִֽינוּ.

segments.id: he:The Cycle of Life/Birkat HaMazon in a House of Mourning:8
segments.html: בָּרוּךְ הוּא וּבָרוּךְ שְׁמוֹ.

segments.id: he:The Cycle of Life/Birkat HaMazon in a House of Mourning:10
segments.html: נַחֵם יהוה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ אֶת אֲבֵלֵי יְרוּשָׁלַֽיִם, וְאֶת הָאֲבֵלִים הַמִּתְאַבְּלִים בָּאֵֽבֶל הַזֶּה. נַחֲמֵם מֵאֶבְלָם וְשַׂמְּחֵם מִיגוֹנָם, כָּאָמוּר: כְּאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר אִמּוֹ תְּנַחֲמֶֽנּוּ, כֵּן אָנֹכִי אֲנַחֶמְכֶם וּבִירוּשָׁלִַֽם תְּנֻחָֽמוּ׃ בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יהוה, מְנַחֵם צִיּוֹן בְּבִנְיַן יְרוּשָׁלָֽיִם. אָמֵן.

segments.id: he:The Cycle of Life/Birkat HaMazon in a House of Mourning:11
segments.html: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יהוה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶֽלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם, הָאֵל אָבִֽינוּ מַלְכֵּֽנוּ אַדִּירֵֽנוּ בּוֹרְאֵֽנוּ גּוֹאֲלֵֽנוּ יוֹצְרֵֽנוּ קְדוֹשֵֽׁנוּ קְדוֹשׁ יַעֲקֹב, רוֹעֵֽנוּ רוֹעֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל, הַמֶּֽלֶךְ הַחַי, הַטּוֹב וְהַמֵּטִיב. אֵל אֱמֶת, דַּיַּן אֱמֶת, שׁוֹפֵט צֶֽדֶק, לוֹקֵֽחַ נְפָשׁוֹת בְּמִשְׁפָּט, וְשַׁלִּיט בְּעוֹלָמוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת בּוֹ כִּרְצוֹנוֹ, כִּי כָל דְּרָכָיו מִשְׁפָּט, וַאֲנַֽחְנוּ עַמּוֹ וַעֲבָדָיו, וְעַל הַכֹּל אֲנַֽחְנוּ חַיָּבִים לְהוֹדוֹת לוֹ וּלְבָרְכוֹ. גּוֹדֵר פִּרְצוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל, הוּא יִגְדֹּר אֶת הַפִּרְצָה הַזֹּאת מֵעָלֵֽינוּ לְחַיִּים וּלְשָׁלוֹם. הוּא יִגְמְלֵֽנוּ לָעַד חֵן וָחֶֽסֶד וְרַחֲמִים וְכָל טוֹב, וּמִכָּל טוּב לְעוֹלָם אַל יְחַסְּרֵֽנוּ.

With your permission,
let us bless the One who comforts mourners

segments.html: Others Blessed be the One who comforts mourners, from whose food we have eaten, and by whose goodness we live.

Leader Blessed be the One who comforts mourners,
from whose food we have eaten, and by whose goodness we live.

segments.id: en:The Cycle of Life/Birkat HaMazon in a House of Mourning:8
segments.html: Blessed be He, and blessed be His name.

segments.id: en:The Cycle of Life/Birkat HaMazon in a House of Mourning:9
segments.html: Continue with Birkat HaMazon on page 978 until “And may Jerusalem” on page 984. Then say:

segments.id: en:The Cycle of Life/Birkat HaMazon in a House of Mourning:10
segments.html: נַחֵם Comfort, O <small>LORD</small> our God, the mourners of Jerusalem and those who mourn here. Grant them consolation in their mourning and gladness in their grief, as it is said, “As a mother comforts her son, so will I comfort you, and in Jerusalem you shall find comfort.” Blessed are You, <small>LORD</small>, who brings comfort to Zion through the rebuilding of Jerusalem. Amen.

segments.id: en:The Cycle of Life/Birkat HaMazon in a House of Mourning:11
segments.html: בָּרוּךְ Blessed are You, <small>LORD</small> our God, King of the Universe – God our Father, our King, our Sovereign, our Creator, our Redeemer, our Maker, our Holy One, the Holy One of Jacob. He is our Shepherd, Israel’s Sheperd, our living King who is good and does good, the true God, the true Judge, who judges righteously and takes back souls in judgment. He rules the world according to His will, for all His ways are just, and we are His people and His servants. For everything, we are duty bound to acknowledge and bless Him. May He who repairs the breaches in Israel, repair this breach in us and grant us life and peace. May He always bestow on us grace, kindness, compassion and all good things. Of all that is good, may He never let us lack.
